correctness.rationale: The quotient is exactly Gaussian/sphere invariant. The real homogeneous square supremum is exactly four Kac boundary paths. For both parity signs, the polygonal partial-sum process converges jointly to independent Brownian motions; cross-covariances have absolute value \(\leq 1/m\) and Gaussian fourth moments prove tightness. Uniform Abel summation gives a sup-s error bounded by \(3\max_j|g_j|/\sqrt m\), tending to zero. Reversing coefficients converges to the time-reversed same Brownian path. The Gaussian coefficient q_m numerator divided by sqrt(m) converges to 1. The limiting maximum is finite and positive a.s.; division and Brownian full support justify the limit and nondegeneracy. The included finite identity checks were successfully executed but are not used as proofs of asymptotics.
